desc: A single polished stone inner-forearm guard with a shallow waist, softly beveled ends, and four hourglass perforations for broad hide bindings; shown as a stiff plate, not a flexible cuff.
historical_anchor: Direct Late Neolithic/Early Bronze Age stone wrist-guard with convex section and four fastening perforations.

desc: A pair of broad materially continuous rawhide strips coiled around empty forearm volumes from wrist toward elbow, with flat overlapping courses and ends buried under the final wrap; no hand shapes.
historical_anchor: A-02 true forearm-wrap family using the hide and sinew sewing vocabulary preserved in Copper Age clothing.

desc: A pair of empty mitten-shaped hide hand coverings with separate thumb bodies, inward fur at the cuffs, and doubled rawhide palms; crude sinew seams only.
historical_anchor: Copper Age hide garments sewn with animal sinew support a conservative cold-weather mitt construction.

desc: A pair of shallow stiff rawhide bands ending at the wrists, each formed as one overlapping continuous cuff; broad plain surfaces, asymmetric repairs, and no forearm extension.
historical_anchor: A-14 short wrist-cuff silhouette grounded in ancient hide cutting and overlapping construction.

desc: A protective pair of short forearm guards, each formed from three broad transverse copper-alloy lames overlapping from wrist toward elbow and laced to one continuous thick leather backing.
historical_anchor: Direct Roman laminated bronze arm-guard fragment from Newstead establishes a genuine protective transverse-lame forearm construction.

desc: A pair of full forearm shells shaped from materially continuous hardened hide, thickened at the outer face, lined by softer leather, and ending cleanly at the wrist.
historical_anchor: Ancient hard and soft leather armor construction provides a direct material and backing precedent.

desc: A pair of full forearm guards ending at the wrist, built as continuous stiff leather cylinders faced by a few broad overlapping hammered copper scales rawhide-laced through the backing.
historical_anchor: Direct ancient overlapping metal scales on continuous leather backing, translated to the copper rung.

desc: A pair of full forearm guards ending at the wrist, built from narrow boiled-hide splints on a soft leather backing and tied by transverse rawhide cords.
historical_anchor: A-06 longitudinal splint bracer, drawing on ancient scale and leather-backing attachment logic.

desc: A pair of rigid full-forearm guards ending at the wrist, with broad overlapping bronze scales completely covering continuous thick leather backings in pierced load-bearing rows.
historical_anchor: Direct ancient overlapping armor scales attached to leather backing, retained as a true armored bracer family.

desc: A pair of plain empty forearm shells in hammered bronze, gently tapered from elbow to wrist with rolled edges, broad leather lining bands, and mostly undecorated metal.
historical_anchor: A-04 paired shaped metal forearm shells using the same hammered sheet and lining logic as Classical Greek limb armor.

desc: A pair of empty heavy leather hand cages enclosing palm, thumb base, and knuckles, each with one compact blunt bronze striking ridge; no spikes or anatomy.
historical_anchor: Direct Roman leather boxing guards excavated at Vindolanda support the complete protective hand-cage family.

desc: A single long arm defense from wrist to upper arm, made from broad transverse bronze splints laced edge-to-edge over one continuous leather sleeve and curving continuously around the elbow.
historical_anchor: Direct bronze laminated Roman arm-guard fragment from Newstead, dated AD 80-180.

desc: A pair of full forearm guards ending at the wrist, made entirely from broad black-red lacquered hard-leather scales rawhide-laced over continuous soft leather sleeves.
historical_anchor: Direct pre-AD Scythian/Subeixi hard-leather scales secured by rawhide laces to soft leather.

desc: A pair of broad rigid copper-alloy wrist cuffs with plain open backs, continuous metal bodies, softly expanded ends, and one narrow bounded gilt edge on each.
historical_anchor: Direct sixth-fifth-century BCE Cypriot gilded bronze bracelet, retained as a complete rigid cuff form.

desc: A single full arm sleeve ending at the wrist, with broad overlapping iron scales stitched in offset rows to one continuous thick leather backing from forearm to upper arm.
historical_anchor: Direct Roman laminated arm-guard artifact supplies the full-arm family; ancient Achaemenid finds establish iron scale on leather as a period construction.

desc: A single broad contiguous inner-forearm plate hammered from raw dark meteoric iron, shallowly waisted with rolled edges and four wide binding slots.
historical_anchor: Direct prehistoric wrist-guard geometry translated into T5 metal as one unarticulated plate.

desc: A severe pair of empty elbow-to-wrist forearm shells hammered from dark meteoric iron, each with a central reinforcing ridge, rolled edge, and broad leather lining bands.
historical_anchor: A-04 shaped metal forearm shells scaled from Classical anatomical greave sheet-metal construction.

desc: A pair of bulky closed shoes with deerskin outer uppers, leather soles, visible bast-fiber inner nets, and dry grass padding; hand-sewn, irregular, and empty.
historical_anchor: Ötzi's Copper Age multilayer footwear: deerskin upper, bast mesh, grass insulation, and leather sole.

desc: A pair of flat coiled-bark soles with one simple woven toe thong and ankle cord each, shown empty and slightly mismatched; no feet or modern stitching.
historical_anchor: Ancient Egyptian woven-fibre sandal with simple sole, toe thong, and ankle strap.

desc: A pair of one-piece rawhide shoes gathered by cord through punched edge holes around a fully closed toe, with soft irregular soles and no separate heel.
historical_anchor: F-04 carbatina/one-piece shoe family, supported by ancient and long-lived gathered-hide construction.

desc: A pair of separate soft hide foot bags with complete closed toes, wrapped at the ankles by two broad fur-backed hide bands; raw sinew ties tucked close.
historical_anchor: Copper Age hide, leather, and sinew clothing technology used for a conservative wrapped closed-foot form.

desc: A pair of flat hide-soled sandals with dense structural rawhide lacing woven continuously around instep and ankle; empty, low, undecorated, and free of metal closures.
historical_anchor: F-02 laced sandal with structural thonging, supported by Late Antique Egyptian cut-and-sewn leather footwear.

desc: A pair of low closed-toe shoes cut from single tan hide sheets, edges gathered over the instep by rawhide lace, flat soft soles, no welt and no shaped modern heel.
historical_anchor: F-04 one-piece gathered leather shoe, a pre-Roman construction family.

desc: A pair of thick folded linen foot wrappings attached to separate oval rawhide soles by sparse edge cords, with complete wrapped toe volumes and tucked ankle ends; no feet.
historical_anchor: F-12 foot wrap with a distinct hard-wearing sole, separated from woven shoes and one-piece felt boots.

desc: A pair of soft ankle-high leather boots with complete rounded toes, side seams and functional rawhide lacing through punched holes; flat soles, no welt or heel block.
historical_anchor: F-06 ancient soft ankle boot construction using hand-cut hide and rawhide lacing.

desc: A pair of empty Roman marching sandals with open cut-leather uppers, dense structural ankle lacing, and heavy flat soles set with sparse hand-driven hobnails; no feet.
historical_anchor: F-03 caliga-type marching sandal, a Roman military footwear family.

desc: A pair of broad layered-leather sandals with complete rounded heel cups, divided toe bands, raw thong stitching through the sole edge, and no metal sole hardware.
historical_anchor: Direct Late Antique Egyptian layered leather sandal with closed heel and thong-stitched sole.

desc: A complete pair of soft closed hide foot bags with flat soles, each continuing into a calf wrap that carries broad vertical boiled-hide splints on continuous leather backing; no anatomy.
historical_anchor: L-10 splint greave joined to an explicit ancient soft-footwear base; leather scale backing supplies the reinforcement logic.

desc: A complete matched pair of plain hammered bronze shin shells worn above simple flat leather thong sandals, with both full soles visible and no generated legs or feet.
historical_anchor: Direct Classical Greek bronze greave construction paired with an explicit ancient sandal read.

desc: A pair of high soft leather riding boots with complete closed toes, flat soles, one broad folded overflap at each calf, and no rigid modern paneling or hardware.
historical_anchor: Direct Parthenon rider relief description records long leather boots with overflaps.

desc: A pair of low closed leather shoes with complete rounded uppers, flat soles, inward fur lining visible only at the openings, and a restrained embossed square-line field across each vamp.
historical_anchor: Direct Graeco-Roman leather shoe from Akhmim with fur lining and embossed square-and-line decoration.

desc: A pair of complete closed low leather shoes with cut openwork uppers and thick flat soles secured by sparse hand-driven hobnails; visibly empty and without modern welt construction.
historical_anchor: Direct Roman British leather shoe with hobnailed sole and openwork upper.

desc: A complete pair of raw dark meteoric-iron shin shells above simple flat hide sandals, every full sole and thong structure visible; rolled shell edges, broad lining holes, no foot plates.
historical_anchor: Direct Classical anatomical greave geometry translated to T5 metal while preserving complete ancient footwear.

desc: A complete pair of soft closed leather calf boots with flat soles and plain flexible feet; broad dark meteoric-iron scales protect the shin courses on continuous leather backing above each ankle.
historical_anchor: Direct ancient iron scales on leather backing combined with a full soft-boot read.

desc: A thick three-ply sinew and hide cord arranged as one shallow horizontal waist loop with a compact tucked knot; no tails, charms, pouches, or fringe.
historical_anchor: C-01 waist cord using Copper Age sinew, leather, and plant-fiber fastening technology.

desc: A broad flat braid of tree-bast cord forming one shallow landscape band with a short overlap buried behind the visible front; worn, serviceable, and free of displayed closure hardware.
historical_anchor: C-01/C-07 supportive cord girdle grounded in Copper Age tree-bast and braided-grass craft.

desc: A narrow continuous rawhide strap doubled once around the waist into a compact shallow band, with the fastening left unseen and no dangling end.
historical_anchor: C-03 plain leather belt using the same prehistoric hide technology preserved in Copper Age clothing.

desc: A broad supportive rawhide waistband with overlapping tapered ends and a scarred plain surface; fastening remains unseen, with no apron panels or hanging parts.
historical_anchor: C-07 broad plain girdle interpreted through prehistoric hide cutting and overlapping construction.

desc: A broad undyed linen band woven in a simple alternating stripe, folded into one shallow waist loop with both short ends tucked fully inside.
historical_anchor: Direct fifth-sixth-century Roman Egyptian linen plain weave with narrow wool stripe fields supplies the textile construction.

desc: A thick rust-red wool sash folded into a compact horizontal band, bound by one internal knot with only a thumb-length tucked end visible; no tassels.
historical_anchor: Direct Roman Egyptian red-wool plain-weave textile with narrow parallel linen stripes supplies the material and weave.

desc: A plain broad leather belt with one long shallow hammered copper terminal facing peened flat across an end field; broad empty strap surfaces and no displayed fastening parts.
historical_anchor: Direct Etruscan pre-AD long bronze belt fitting supplies the bounded terminal geometry.

desc: A broad continuous vegetable-tanned leather band with hand-cut edges, an uninterrupted plain face, a shallow overlap, and fastening left unseen.
historical_anchor: C-03 plain leather band informed by the organic belt bodies that carried ancient metal fittings.

desc: A broad dark leather band faced by a small hand-varied set of broad plain bronze plates, each visibly peened through the backing; shallow, load-bearing, and mostly undecorated.
historical_anchor: C-04 plaque belt anchored by the long Etruscan bronze belt fitting dated ca. 625-600 BCE.

desc: A horizontal leather military belt reinforced by a few irregular broad bronze stiffeners peened through continuous backing, with an uninterrupted shallow silhouette and fastening left unseen.
historical_anchor: C-05 segmented military belt informed by Late Roman cast belt plates and attachment studs.

desc: A sturdy broad leather waist band with one broad flat suspension loop held flush against the lower edge, an uninterrupted upper band, and fastening left unseen.
historical_anchor: Direct pre-Roman Iron Age sword scabbard has a broad rectangular suspension loop; intake 165 confirms the desired shallow belt-first silhouette.

desc: A broad continuous leather girdle faced across its front half by one long thin hammered bronze sheet with softly rolled horizontal edges and sparse peened attachment points; fastening unseen.
historical_anchor: Direct Etruscan bronze belt fitting dated ca. 625-600 BCE and measuring 26.3 cm wide.

desc: A broad black-red lacquered leather waist band reinforced by one restrained row of hard-leather scales rawhide-laced flat to continuous backing; no displayed closure.
historical_anchor: C-07 supportive girdle combined with direct pre-AD Scythian/Subeixi hard-leather scale construction.

desc: A heavy plain oxhide belt with one broad gilt-bronze facing plate peened flat across a rigid front field, leaving most leather visible; fastening remains unseen and no hanging gear appears.
historical_anchor: Direct fifth-century Late Roman gilt copper-alloy belt plate and attachment rivets support the bounded prestige facing.

desc: A massive but shallow dark leather warbelt with a few broad plain raw meteoric-iron plates peened through continuous backing, broad empty fields, and fastening left unseen.
historical_anchor: C-04 plaque-belt structure built by ancient riveting and leather backing, using Verdigris raw meteoritic iron.

desc: A severe double-layer hide girdle reinforced by short overlapping dark meteoric-iron segments across the front half, all edges rolled or bound and fastening left unseen.
historical_anchor: C-05 segmented military belt translated into a restrained T5 ancient-workshop construction.
